auth.header: Send the generated application capability in the HTTP Authorization header using the Bearer scheme.
auth.mcp_access: The standard Wizard gateway can call the two public identity/status tools without an app capability; no conversation read/send or signer tool exists. Browser-origin checks still apply.
auth.browser_origins: Exact comma-separated MESSENGER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS; no permissive CORS. Non-browser clients may omit Origin. Cross-site browser requests are rejected.
auth.secret_transport: The owner passphrase travels only in an authenticated HTTPS JSON body and private provider stdin, never URLs, logs or browser storage. Private-key import is disabled.
auth.browser_session: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict app-path cookie; cookie writes also require exact Origin and X-Messenger-CSRF. Machine bearer never appears in the view.
auth.initial_browser_access: Machine-issued tickets are setup-only, never unlocked owner sessions. Exchanges are rejected after an account or owner verifier exists. Machine-issued launcher tickets cannot establish the first owner verifier. Initial enrollment requires an independently provisioned BrowserAuth.ticket(bootstrap=True); no machine-bearer HTTP route issues enrollment authority. Tickets belong only in the URL fragment. Existing accounts require owner passphrase/passkey proof. Bearer-authenticated HTML never sets an owner cookie. Pre-v2 sessions and tickets are invalidated on upgrade.
auth.existing_browser_access: POST /api/view/unlock proves the dedicated passphrase against a salted scrypt verifier and unlocks the provider; it cannot create/import an account. Six failed guesses per minute are rate-limited. No anonymous initial-account creation.
auth.stored_browser_auth: Browser-auth stores only ticket/session hashes and a salted passphrase verifier; no plaintext passphrase, cookie capability or message body. Atomic 0600 app-data file. Optional local trusted-owner unlock stores a separate AES-GCM envelope, never plaintext.
auth.local_trusted_wizard_owner: Disabled unless MESSENGER_TRUST_WIZARD_OWNER=1 with separate private proof/wrapping key files outside data. Every non-machine API call additionally requires a short-lived one-use HMAC proof from the authenticated owner gateway. All bearer modes remain agent-only. One verified passphrase unlock with explicit remember_wizard:true seals a remembered unlock; signed GET /api/view/session can reopen the original encrypted vault after restart. Lock durably forgets it. No account or enrollment reset. See TRUSTED-WIZARD-OWNER.md.

agent_policy.authority: Only an authenticated owner browser session with Origin and CSRF can change policy. Machine bearers cannot change policy, unlock sessions, or link/manage provider accounts in any mode.
agent_policy.compatibility: Legacy until-only grants fail closed to no_access. Legacy minutes-only enabling requests are rejected; minutes:0 still revokes. Optional explicit-mode expiry is 1..1440 minutes; expiry returns to no_access.
agent_policy.semantics: no_access permits health/status/public identity and setup-only launch tickets. read_only additionally permits explicitly allowlisted conversation reads. draft_only adds local draft create/update only, not previews, sends, reactions, read receipts, typing, edits, deletes, invites, logins, account links, translation calls, or provider writes. full_access enables explicitly allowlisted conversation mutations, never owner-control routes. Unknown routes fail closed.
agent_policy.boundary: Application defense in depth only; not protection against host root. Independently administered sender enforcement is a separate integration.

setup_semantics: No identity is created automatically. A dedicated vault passphrase of at least 16 characters is needed to create/unlock. Keyring remains encrypted at rest. Restart always relocks. account_configured reports whether an identity exists; ready may have identity=null when a new vault has only been unlocked. The one messaging key is separate from Wizard root signing.

routes.notes: Any-file support requested by James, 26 Oct 2026. Files keep the basename after / or backslash, remove Unicode control/format/surrogate characters and leading spaces/dots, collapse whitespace, and cap the name at 120 characters while retaining the final extension (an extension alone over 119 characters is truncated). Empty names become file. MIME comes from magic bytes (including PDF and ZIP), never the client Content-Type or extension; unknown bytes use application/octet-stream. Synapse receives the fixed filename attachment. Telegram, WhatsApp and Signal only. Handles are person-bound, expire after one hour and are consumed on send. Existing image/voice results are unchanged.

mcp_media.levels: read_only and up (same capability as GET /api/unified/media/{id}, the view's own media route; No access refuses before any fetch)
mcp_media.reference: messenger_read_thread messages with media carry attachment {index:0, kind: image|sticker|video|audio|voice|file, mime, name, size, w, h, duration, fetch:{tool:'messenger_get_attachment', chat_id, message_id, index}}; never an mxc URI or homeserver token
mcp_media.get_attachment: messenger_get_attachment {chat_id, message_id, index?}: the message must belong to chat_id (otherwise not_found). Images use the view's media cache/fetch (full, else the homeserver 800 px preview; Pillow downscales to 1600 px when present) and return MCP content [text JSON metadata, {type:'image', data: base64, mimeType}] capped at 1.5 MiB; larger pictures return metadata with image:'not_returned'. Non-images return metadata only (no download), except text files up to 64 KiB, returned as text. Metadata carries the untrusted-content note.

mcp_attachments.levels: draft_only and draft_and_send (same capability as PUT/DELETE /api/drafts/{id}/attachments)
mcp_attachments.tools: messenger_create_draft and messenger_update_draft accept attachments, stored with the text in the same single revision (a viewer never sees a text-only or partly attached draft); messenger_attach_to_draft adds all its files in one revision; messenger_remove_draft_attachment removes by id. Every edit is revision-fenced.
mcp_attachments.item: {"path": file inside the shared folder} or {"base64": bytes, "name": optional display name}; 1..10 per call, 10 per draft, 25 MiB each, 100 MiB across all drafts; type sniffed from bytes
mcp_attachments.shared_folder: MESSENGER_AGENT_FILES_DIR (default /attachments, mounted read-only; Wizard: Files Messenger/Attachments). Relative paths, or absolute paths under MESSENGER_AGENT_FILES_HOST_DIR; .., other absolute paths, symlinks out and non-regular files are refused (invalid_attachment) before any draft write.
mcp_attachments.body_limit: POST /mcp accepts up to 36 MiB only with a valid per-agent key or the gateway's grant; otherwise 64 KiB.

agent_keys.mcp_auth: Per-agent key in the Authorization header of POST /mcp. Without one (or with the shared Wizard app key) /mcp exposes only messenger_status and messenger_public_identity.
agent_keys.sending: No MCP send tool for any key or Wizard agent. Only the owner's signed-in browser session sends a draft (preview then send, revision-fenced).
agent_keys.reuse: agent_keys.py is app-agnostic (levels -> read/draft/send capabilities); another app supplies its own route/tool map.

parent_owned: Wizard app-manager and private proxy deployment; view, session bridge and API now ship inside the same Messenger image
unified_privacy: Matrix and Telegram history and translations are plaintext in app-local SQLite. Telegram cloud chats are not end-to-end encrypted. Text selected for translation is sent only to Tinfoil. Existing Marmot keyring/history is unchanged.

wizard_agents.what: The Wizard's own agents (Agent Service registry ids; main agent 'hermes'), each with one owner-picked level. No key to create or copy.
wizard_agents.gateway_auth: POST /mcp with X-Wizard-Grant: <the Agent Service gateway's app grant key> (wizard-os spec/PERMISSIONS.md layer 2). Messenger hashes it and accepts it only when it matches the from: host:agent-service row (outside the app-ID namespace) in the incoming list of its grants file ($WIZARD_GRANTS_FILE, written by the App Manager); Authorization is not used for it. Accepted on /mcp only; any other route refuses a request carrying it (401). A wrong or other app's grant names nobody. The grants file's enforce flag is ignored (Messenger is not enforce-ready).
wizard_agents.agent_identity: X-Wizard-Agent (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$) and URI-encoded X-Wizard-Agent-Label, trusted only together with the gateway's grant. The gateway authenticates each agent with that agent's own gateway token.
wizard_agents.levels: no_access (default, also for unknown agents), read_only, draft_only. Never draft_and_send.
wizard_agents.tools_list: The gateway gets the full message tool list (it caches one list for all agents); each tools/call is checked against the named agent's level. A gateway call naming no agent runs nothing.
wizard_agents.storage: /data/wizard-agents.json, mode 0600; corrupt store fails closed (every agent No access).
wizard_agents.owner_listing: GET /api/view/agents adds wizard_agents (main agent always listed), wizard_levels and gateway_connected.
